python3 - <<'EOF'
from pathlib import Path
p = Path("tests/acceptance/W1-26/README.md")
s = p.read_text()
marker = "## Fixture: kernel skills copied (DEC-439)"
assert s.count(marker) == 1
section = r'''## A commit citing an unrecorded decision (DEC-463) — follow-up round

Added by the Independent Test Designer (MR-3) for owner decision DEC-463, before implementation.
`test_w1_26_decision_citations.py`, 45 cases.

**S9** "Flags a commit that cites a decision id missing from the decision register at that commit: a decision is
recorded before the change it authorises (DEC-463) [CAP-38.b]".

### What is settled, and from what

| Point | Settled | Source |
|---|---|---|
| The decision register in a project | The decision files of the project: every Markdown file whose frontmatter has `type: decision`, or an `id` in the `decision_id` grammar, in any folder. A decision is recorded when such a file carries its id. Read by frontmatter, never by prose. | `tests/acceptance/W1-11/README.md` ("A decision file"), DEC-329, DEC-387 |
| The register as one file of headed entries | **Open: package P-1.** No source gives a checker that form. It is this repository's present state only (Charter v5 names `docs/DECISION_REGISTER.md`; DEC-274: "decisions are headings in the register, not files"; W1-11's README: the two series "are not both files yet"). No case here uses it. | as named |
| What a citation is | A whole word in the `decision_id` grammar of the kernel's shared definitions (`ADR-` or `DEC-` and three or more digits), in the commit's message: subject, body or trailers. Lower case, fewer digits, another prefix (`CAP-38`, `W1-26`, `L-0900`, `DP-900`, a ticket id) or a longer word around it is no citation. | DEC-227 and `tests/acceptance/W1-08/README.md` (reading 11: one shared `decision_id`), DEC-182 (trailers are part of the message) |
| The changed text | Not read. DEC-463 says "a commit that cites": the commit speaks through its message. An id named by a file is that file's reference (the graph's dangling reference of DEC-274), whoever commits it. | DEC-463, DEC-274 |
| "At that commit" | The register in the tree of the same commit. A commit that adds the decision and cites it is not flagged. A commit citing a decision that a later commit adds stays flagged. A decision present at the citing commit and removed later does not flag that commit; a commit citing it after the removal is flagged. A commit on a merged branch is judged by its own tree, not the merge's. | The KPI line ("missing from the decision register at that commit"), DEC-463 ("recorded before the change it authorises") |
| Which commits are judged | **Open: package P-2.** DEC-463 says "from now on" and accepts seven late records by name; no source says how `gov check` knows where "now" is, and `gov check` takes no range (`--list`, `--json`; DEC-186). W1-11's README leaves it to this design ("W1-26 may need a range or a baseline"). Every project of these cases records no base and dates every commit after 2026-10-07, so each of its commits is judged under every option of P-2. No case plants history from before the rule. | DEC-463, DEC-186, `tests/acceptance/W1-11/README.md` ("Notes for the lead") |
| The form of the check | A declared check in the kernel's checks (`id`, `family`, `tier`, `severity`, `command`), id `core-decision-citations` (the ticket's path is `template/governance/kernel/checks/core-*`). `gov check` runs it because it is declared. | KPI S7, the ticket's `allowed_paths` |
| Family | "authority/role limits": the rule is about what authorises a change, and this suite already places the decision checker's findings there. | KPI S7 (the 17 families), CAP-01, `test_w1_26_decisions.py` |
| Severity | `warning`: YELLOW, never a hard block. The owner's word is "flags"; every other line of this ticket says "Fails". A commit once made cannot be mended (DEC-182: history is not rewritten), so a hard block would stay red for ever and stop every merge under DEC-466. | DEC-463, DEC-182, DEC-466, CAP-39.d |
| Fail-opens | No repository, a repository without a commit, a git that fails, a history that cannot be read: the unmeasured answer of this suite (`"unmeasured": true`, a reason, exit 1). A decision file of a judged commit that cannot be read: exit 1 and the file is named. None is clean, and none is the not-applicable answer: DEC-447 gives that answer to the audit check alone. | DEC-425, DEC-447, DEC-387, "Validator exit codes" above |

### The interface the cases fix

| What | Value |
|---|---|
| Declaration | exactly one declaration with `id: core-decision-citations` under `template/governance/kernel/checks/`; `family` "authority/role limits" (compared as DEC-436 compares); `severity: warning`; no `allows-not-applicable` |
| Command | the declaration's `command`, run by a shell in the project's root with this worktree's `src/` on `PYTHONPATH`; its name is the engineer's |
| Output | one JSON object on stdout |
| A flagged commit | one entry of `findings`: `{"code": "DECISION_UNRECORDED", "commit": "<the full commit id>", "decision": "<the id>"}`, one for each commit and id (an id written twice in one message is one finding); other keys are free |
| Exit codes | 0 clean; 1 findings or unmeasured; never 2 |
| Through `gov check` | the check's result has `id` `core-decision-citations`; `status` YELLOW with a flagged commit, GREEN on a clean history, never GREEN over a register it cannot read |

A case that expects "not flagged" also holds one flagged commit (it cites `DEC-900`, recorded nowhere) and
asserts the exact set of findings. So it is red until the check exists, and a check that reports nothing does
not pass it.

### Cases

| Group | Cases | What | Red reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| The declaration | 3 | family; severity `warning`; no `allows-not-applicable` | no declaration `core-decision-citations` |
| An unrecorded citation is flagged | 8 | in the subject, the body, a trailer (3); exit 1; an `ADR-` id; two ids are two findings and a repeated id one; the unrecorded id alone beside a recorded one; every citing commit, not the last alone | as above |
| At that commit | 6 | a clean history is clean (exit 0, no finding); record and citation in one commit; recorded by a later commit; removed later; cited after removal; a merged branch's commit by its own tree | as above |
| What the register is | 4 | a typed file in `docs/adr/`, a typed file in another folder, a file with no `type` and an id in the grammar (3); an id named in prose or in another decision's `supersedes` is not recorded | as above |
| What a citation is | 14 | thirteen id-like words that are no decision id; an id in the changed text alone | as above |
| Fail-opens | 6 | no repository; no commit; a stand-in `git` that fails; a missing commit object; a decision file with frontmatter not closed or not YAML (2) | as above |
| Through `gov check` | 4 | YELLOW with a flagged commit; GREEN on a clean history; the family YELLOW; never GREEN over an unreadable register | `gov check gives no result for the check 'core-decision-citations'` |

Observed red before implementation, 2026-10-07: 41 errors at the `declaration` fixture (`0 check declarations with
id 'core-decision-citations' under template/governance/kernel/checks/`) and 4 failures in the `gov check` cases
(`gov check gives no result for the check 'core-decision-citations'`).

| Covers id | Tests |
|---|---|
| DEC-463 (a decision is recorded before the change it authorises) | `test_w1_26_decision_citations.py` |
| CAP-38.b (a declared check of a named family) | `test_w1_26_decision_citations.py` (the declaration, through `gov check`) |
| DEC-425, DEC-447 (unmeasured, never green; not-applicable for the audit check alone) | `test_w1_26_decision_citations.py` (fail-opens) |

### Open packages

**P-1 (P1). Does the check know a register that is one file of headed entries?**
The sources define decisions as files (W1-11). This repository records them as headings `### DEC-nnn — title` in
`docs/DECISION_REGISTER.md`, and DEC-466 has `gov check` run here before every merge. A check that knows files
alone flags every commit of this repository that cites a `DEC-` id (DEC-274: every such reference dangles), so here
it measures nothing.
- (a) **Recommended.** Both forms. A decision is recorded at a commit when a decision file of that commit's tree
  carries its id, or when a register file of that tree has a heading that opens with the id. The project names its
  register file (one line of project configuration under `governance/project/`); no path of this repository is
  written into the kernel. With no register file named, files alone.
- (b) Files alone. The check stays yellow in this repository until its decisions are records; DEC-467's baseline
  would carry it.
- (c) Both forms, with `docs/DECISION_REGISTER.md` and `### <id>` fixed in the kernel. Simplest; it puts this
  repository's layout into every adopter's kernel.
Needed with (a) or (c), then written as cases: the heading grammar (level, what may follow the id), and whether an
id in a heading inside a fenced block or a table row counts (recommended: a heading line outside a fence only).

**P-2 (P1). Which commits are judged, and what of the commits made before the rule?**
- (a) **Recommended.** A base commit recorded in the project (under `governance/project/`): the commits reachable
  from `HEAD` and not from the base are judged, merges and the commits they bring included. With no base recorded,
  every commit reachable from `HEAD`. For this repository the base is the commit that records DEC-463
  (`46ec8da3`); the seven late records lie before it. A base that is not a commit of the repository, or not an
  ancestor of `HEAD`, is unmeasured.
- (b) A date in the kernel (2026-10-07). Dates are the committer's to choose, and the kernel would carry this
  repository's date into every adopter.
- (c) A range argument to `gov check`. It changes the command's interface (DEC-186), and a check before a merge
  would judge only what its caller thinks to pass.
- (d) Every commit, and a list of accepted findings by commit and id (as DEC-467 does for red checks). Exact, and a
  hand-maintained list (failure KPI 2).
Cases that wait for the answer: commits before the base are not flagged; a base that cannot be resolved; a shallow
clone whose boundary hides judged commits.

### Not tested

- The headed register (P-1) and history from before the rule (P-2).
- A decision's `status`: whether a `PROPOSED` or `SUPERSEDED` decision counts as recorded. The KPI says "missing
  from the decision register"; the cases record with `ACTIVE`.
- A range written in prose ("DEC-460 to DEC-466"): both ends are citations by the grammar; the ids between are not
  read.
- An id with a prefix before it (`X-DEC-900`) or a suffix after a hyphen (`DEC-900-draft`).
- A decision file with the extension `.MD` or `.markdown` (DEC-387's residual), and one moved between two commits.
- Notes (`git notes`) and tag messages: the commit's own message alone.
- Whether an unreadable decision file is reported as a finding or as unmeasured: the cases fix exit 1 and the
  file's name in the output.
- Latency on a long history.

'''
s = s.replace(marker, section + marker)
s = s.replace("| `test_w1_26_not_applicable.py` | 21 | S2, S7 (DEC-447) |\n",
              "| `test_w1_26_not_applicable.py` | 21 | S2, S7 (DEC-447) |\n| `test_w1_26_decision_citations.py` | 45 | S9 (DEC-463) |\n")
s = s.replace("| **S8** \"Fails a record that changes authority class without a decision\" [CAP-01.c] | `test_w1_26_authority.py` (5) | `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` |\n",
              "| **S8** \"Fails a record that changes authority class without a decision\" [CAP-01.c] | `test_w1_26_authority.py` (5) | `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` |\n| **S9** \"Flags a commit that cites a decision id missing from the decision register at that commit\" (DEC-463) [CAP-38.b] | `test_w1_26_decision_citations.py` (45) | no declaration `core-decision-citations`; see \"A commit citing an unrecorded decision\" |\n")
p.write_text(s)
EOF
git diff --stat; cat "$TMPDIR/w1-26-before.txt" 2>/dev/null

**Counts:** before `212 passed, 1 skipped`; after `4 failed, 212 passed, 1 skipped, 41 errors`. All 45 new cases are red and nothing else moved.

## Packages (both P1, both open; no case guesses them)

**P-1. Does the check know a register that is one file of headed entries?**
The sources define decisions only as files (W1-11 README, "A decision file"). The headed form is this repository's present state (Charter v5; DEC-274; W1-11 README: the two series "are not both files yet"), and no source gives a checker that form. A files-only check flags every commit here that cites a `DEC-` id, so in this repository it measures nothing.
- **(a) Recommended:** both forms. The project names its register file in one line of configuration under `governance/project/`; with none named, files alone. No path of this repository goes into the kernel.
- (b) Files alone; the check stays yellow here until decisions are records.
- (c) Both forms, with `docs/DECISION_REGISTER.md` and `### <id>` fixed in the kernel.
- With (a) or (c) I also need the heading grammar: level, what may follow the id, and whether a heading inside a fence counts.

**P-2. Which commits are judged, and what of commits made before the rule?**
DEC-463 says "from now on" and accepts seven late records by name. No source says how the check knows where "now" is, `gov check` takes no range (DEC-186), and W1-11's README leaves it to this design.
- **(a) Recommended:** a base commit recorded in the project. Commits reachable from `HEAD` and not from the base are judged, merges and what they bring included; with no base, the whole history. Here the base would be `46ec8da3`, the commit that records DEC-463. A base that cannot be resolved is unmeasured.
- (b) A date in the kernel. Dates are the committer's to choose, and it carries this repository's date to every adopter.
- (c) A range argument to `gov check`. It changes the command's interface.
- (d) Every commit plus a list of accepted findings, which is a hand-maintained list (failure KPI 2).
- Waiting on the answer: commits before the base are not flagged; an unresolvable base; a shallow clone.
- Every project in the cases records no base and dates its judged commits 2026-10-09, so the cases hold under (a), (b) and (d). Under (c) they gain the argument.

## Settled, with source

| Point | Settled | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Register in a project | Decision files: Markdown with frontmatter `type: decision`, or an `id` in the `decision_id` grammar, in any folder; read by frontmatter, never prose | W1-11 README, DEC-329, DEC-387 |
| Citation | A whole word in the kernel's shared `decision_id` grammar (`ADR-`/`DEC-` and three or more digits) in the commit message: subject, body, trailers | DEC-227, W1-08 README reading 11, DEC-182 |
| Changed text | Not read: "a commit that cites" is its message; an id named in a file is that file's dangling reference | DEC-463, DEC-274 |
| "At that commit" | The tree of the same commit, including for a commit on a merged side branch | KPI line, DEC-463 |
| Form | A declared kernel check, id `core-decision-citations`; the command is the engineer's and the cases read it from the declaration | KPI line 7, the ticket's `core-*` path |
| Family | "authority/role limits" | KPI line 7, CAP-01, `test_w1_26_decisions.py` |
| Severity | `warning` (YELLOW) | "flags" against "Fails" on every other line; DEC-182 with DEC-466 |
| Fail-opens | No repository, no commit, a failing git, an unreadable history: the suite's unmeasured answer (exit 1, a reason). An unreadable decision file: exit 1 with the file named. Never exit 2 or not-applicable | DEC-425, DEC-447 |

Three of these are my reading rather than a quoted sentence, so the owner may want to confirm them:
- **Severity.** W1-11's KPI also says "flags" and its findings are red in this suite. I chose warning because history is not rewritten (DEC-182), so a hard block could never be cleared and would stop every merge under DEC-466. Five cases depend on it: the declared severity, the two YELLOW cases through `gov check`, and, through the fixed `findings`/unmeasured exit code 1, the "exit 1" case and the unmeasured cases.
- **Family.** "graph integrity" is the other candidate (a dangling reference). Two cases depend on it.
- **Changed text not read.** One case depends on it.

The cases also fix the finding shape: `{"code": "DECISION_UNRECORDED", "commit": <full id>, "decision": <id>}`, one per commit and id, in one JSON object on stdout; exit 0 clean, 1 for findings or unmeasured.

## Cases and red reasons

| Group | Cases | What |
|---|---|---|
| Declaration | 3 | family; severity `warning`; no `allows-not-applicable` |
| Unrecorded citation flagged | 8 | subject, body, trailer; exit 1; an `ADR-` id; two ids give two findings and a repeated id one; only the unrecorded id beside a recorded one; every citing commit, not the last alone |
| At that commit | 6 | clean history (exit 0, no finding); record and citation in one commit; recorded by a later commit; removed later; cited after removal; a merged branch's commit by its own tree |
| What the register is | 4 | typed file in `docs/adr/`; typed file elsewhere; no `type` with an id in the grammar; an id in prose or in another decision's `supersedes` is not recorded |
| What a citation is | 14 | 13 id-like words (`CAP-38`, `W1-26`, `L-0900`, `DP-900`, `FAIL-0900`, `PROJ-aaaa`, `DEC-90`, `ADR-9`, `dec-901`, `DEC901`, `DEC_901`, `CODEC-901`, `DEC-901x`); an id in the changed text alone |
| Fail-opens | 6 | no repository; no commit; stand-in `git` that fails; missing commit object; frontmatter not closed; frontmatter not YAML |
| Through `gov check` | 4 | YELLOW when flagged; GREEN when clean; family YELLOW; never GREEN over an unreadable register |

- **41 errors** stop at the `declaration` fixture: `0 check declarations with id 'core-decision-citations' under template/governance/kernel/checks/ (expected exactly one)`.
- **4 failures** are the `gov check` cases: `gov check gives no result for the check 'core-decision-citations'`.

Every "not flagged" case also holds one flagged commit citing `DEC-900` and asserts the exact set of findings, so a check that reports nothing cannot pass it. The one case with a loose assertion is the last: "never GREEN" allows YELLOW or RED, because DEC-425 states only that.

Not tested, and listed in the README: decision `status`, prose ranges such as "DEC-460 to DEC-466", `X-DEC-900` and `DEC-900-draft`, `.MD` files, moved files, latency.

## Two things to know

- The worktree shows untracked entries I did not create and did not commit: `.bashrc`, `.gitconfig`, `.idea`, `.mcp.json`, `.vscode`, `docs/source` and similar. The containment hook reports them as "left in place".
- The full run that gave the counts preceded a final README-only edit (the red-reason paragraph); no test file changed after it.
